exercises.name: Angled chest-pec curl
exercises.note: Grip a fixed vertical support (rack upright, door frame, sturdy tree). Lean back so your body is on a 30–45° diagonal, feet planted forward. With your free hand, perform a slow dumbbell curl — the diagonal angle shifts the resistance line across the pec, creating a deep stretch and contraction you cannot replicate from standing. Keep the elbow path slightly out from the body. Switch sides.

exercises.name: DB bench press or DB floor press
exercises.note: Bench if available, floor press if not. Full chest. Elbows at 45° from torso — not flared wide. Lower slow, press explosively.

exercises.name: Bent-over DB row
exercises.note: Hinge at hips, flat back, pull elbow straight back past the hip. The single most important back exercise in this program. Squeeze at the top for one count.

exercises.name: DB shoulder press
exercises.note: Seated or standing. Press straight up, slight forward lean at top. Don't arch the lower back to grind out reps — stop clean.

exercises.name: Lateral raises
exercises.note: Light weight, slow tempo. Lead with the elbow, not the hand. Stop at shoulder height. These are the secret weapon for shoulder width and injury prevention.

exercises.name: Rear delt fly
exercises.note: Hinge forward, arms hanging, open wide like wings. Pause at the top. Critical for posture and rotator cuff health — especially important for a runner carrying a vest 20+ miles.

exercises.name: Superset: DB curl + overhead tricep extension

exercises.name: Hammer curl
exercises.note: Neutral grip (palms facing each other). Targets brachialis and brachioradialis — the muscles that fill in the arm between bicep and forearm. Often neglected.

lift.title: Daily Upper Body — One Workout, Every Day
lift.note: Same workout every day. No decisions. Memorize it once, execute it forever. 25–35 min. Rest 45–60 sec between sets. On peak running weeks (12–18), drop to 2 sets per exercise. Phase scaling: 2 sets, light weight, 20–25 min max. Just keeping the neuromuscular pattern alive.
lift.philosophy: Consistent daily stimulus at moderate volume beats variable high-volume sessions for both muscle retention during endurance training and ADHD-friendly execution. Your nervous system learns the movement patterns deeply, decisions go to zero, and you show up.

exercises.name: Angled chest-pec curl
exercises.note: Grip a fixed vertical support (rack upright, door frame, sturdy tree). Lean back so your body is on a 30–45° diagonal, feet planted forward. With your free hand, perform a slow dumbbell curl — the diagonal angle shifts the resistance line across the pec, creating a deep stretch and contraction you cannot replicate from standing. Keep the elbow path slightly out from the body. Switch sides.

exercises.name: DB bench press or DB floor press
exercises.note: Bench if available, floor press if not. Full chest. Elbows at 45° from torso — not flared wide. Lower slow, press explosively.

exercises.name: Bent-over DB row
exercises.note: Hinge at hips, flat back, pull elbow straight back past the hip. The single most important back exercise in this program. Squeeze at the top for one count.

exercises.name: DB shoulder press
exercises.note: Seated or standing. Press straight up, slight forward lean at top. Don't arch the lower back to grind out reps — stop clean.

exercises.name: Lateral raises
exercises.note: Light weight, slow tempo. Lead with the elbow, not the hand. Stop at shoulder height. These are the secret weapon for shoulder width and injury prevention.

exercises.name: Rear delt fly
exercises.note: Hinge forward, arms hanging, open wide like wings. Pause at the top. Critical for posture and rotator cuff health — especially important for a runner carrying a vest 20+ miles.
